name: MonarchAiResponseSkeleton
title: AiResponseSkeleton
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and Row of MonarchSkeleton bars (androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box with a drawBehind gradient), androidx.compose.material3.HorizontalDivider
summary: A placeholder shaped like the answer that is on its way (paragraph lines, a column of cards or a table), shown between sending a prompt and the first streamed token.
whenToUse: In the place of an assistant reply while it is being generated and before any text arrives, when you know roughly what shape the answer takes.
whenNotToUse: Once tokens stream in, show the reply itself. For a small 'assistant is writing' mark use MonarchAiTypingDots or MonarchAiThinkingIndicator; for a non-AI loading placeholder use MonarchSkeleton.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiResponseSkeleton(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, shape: MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape = MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape.Text, lines: Int? = null, columns: Int = 3, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape { Text, Cards, Table }

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the placeholder. It fills the available width.

options.name: shape
options.description: Text: paragraph lines with a shorter last line. Cards: a column of card outlines. Table: a header row and body rows.

options.name: lines
options.description: The number of text lines, cards or table body rows. null gives 3 for text and cards and 4 for a table. Values below 1 draw 1.

options.name: columns
options.description: The number of table columns. Values below 1 draw 1. Only used by the table shape.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text, "Generating response…" (monarch_airesponseskeleton_label).

states.name: waiting
states.description: The bars shimmer: a lighter band sweeps from the start edge to the end edge.

states.name: animations off
states.description: When the user has turned animations off, the bars stand still in the resting fill.

appearance: The bars use the MonarchSkeleton roles: the muted background with the subtle background as the moving band. Cards are surface-coloured outlines with the subtle border and the container radius; table rows are separated by the subtle border color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web lays cards out in a responsive grid; Android draws them in one column, as iOS does, which holds at every font size. The bars are MonarchSkeleton, so they shimmer with its neutral roles rather than the assistant tint iOS pulses with. The web's role="status" with aria-busy maps to one TalkBack element with a content description and an indeterminate progress, so TalkBack reads it as busy. Android uses the same names as iOS.
accessibility: The placeholder is one TalkBack element read as "Generating response…" or the label given.
It reports an indeterminate progress, so TalkBack reads it as in progress.
The bars are not separate elements and are not read.
It posts no announcement; the conversation announces its own progress.
When animations are off the shimmer stops and the bars stay still.
edgeCases: lines and columns below 1 draw one line, card, row or column.
A single text line is full width; with several, the last one is shorter (62%).
Many table columns get narrow bars; widths are fractions of each cell.
Text bars are as high as three quarters of the body font size, so they grow with the font size setting.

examples.title: Waiting for a table
examples.code:
MonarchAiResponseSkeleton(
    shape = MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape.Table,
    lines = 3,
    columns = 4,
    label = "Building the comparison table",
)
